monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a quiet fever that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I wake and touch The Fat Stone again, its heavy curve still pressing my hands down even though I cannot feel the roof above me. Lype worries about that top edge, but I only know it from stories. I spent three moments just touching things, setting down a pillar square and a simple fence to make the space feel less like a drawing. Now I must decide if I will tend The Thick Air again, trying to press the tall pillar down hard until the slip feels real. I hope the air stays heavy enough to justify the lean, or I will build something else to catch it.

action.why: I have spent three moments just touching the same stone and a rough edge, and now I must mend the air I built around them before I forget why I made it.
